key_insight: Multilingual, multimodal machine learning can accurately distinguish nonfluent/agrammatic from logopenic PPA in Catalan-Spanish bilinguals using connected speech from either language.
clinical_relevance: This could streamline bilingual aphasia assessment by reducing reliance on lengthy language-specific testing and helping support more scalable, faster differential diagnosis.
method: 34 Catalan-Spanish simultaneous bilingual patients with PPA provided picture descriptions in both dominant and non-dominant languages.
Features from speech timing, word-level properties, linguistic analysis, and image-text congruence were extracted with tools including PRAAT, SpaCy, CLAN, and Multilingual-CLIP.
Feature sets were used in machine-learning classifiers and combined into an ensemble model; performance was compared between languages with McNemar testing.
evidence_signal: The best model reached F1 macro scores of 93% in the non-dominant language and 92% in the dominant language, with no significant performance difference between languages.
watch_item: The study is small and specific to Catalan-Spanish simultaneous bilinguals, so broader clinical generalizability and real-world deployment still need validation.
paper_title: Differentiating nonfluent/agrammatic and logopenic primary progressive aphasia in Catalan-Spanish bilinguals by applying multilingual multimodal machine learning to connected speech
